themes_detail.label: Curb Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 2300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting rapid street deterioration or a new enforcement/complaint awareness pattern in Hunts Point.
evidence: 3 curb condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 8.69 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Curb complaints were near-zero baseline for 8 weeks prior, now suddenly clustering
reporting_angles: What triggered the sudden surge in curb complaints—are residents newly aware of a pothole/damage epidemic, or did conditions deteriorate overnight?
Are sanitation or Parks Dept. operations changing, or is this a seasonal spring thaw effect?

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Spike
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints jumped to 6 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 1.2 per week over 8 weeks—a 380% increase (z-score: 4.36)—suggesting potential HVAC failures, mold issues, or building envelope breaches across multiple residential units.
evidence: 6 indoor air quality complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.36, classified as high severity
Coincides with broader air quality spike (4 complaints 2 weeks ago vs 0.6 baseline), suggesting district-wide air quality event
reporting_angles: Are landlords in rent-stabilized buildings failing to maintain HVAC systems?
Is a localized pollution source (industrial, traffic, waste facility) degrading indoor air in neighboring buildings?
Interview residents filing complaints to identify whether issue is isolated to one building or spread across multiple properties

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Surge
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints rose to 7 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 1.2 per week over 8 weeks—a 460% spike (z-score: 6.93)—indicating a potential outbreak or heightened pest activity in the Hunts Point area.
evidence: 7 rodent complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 6.93, classified as high severity
Coincides with 502 total unsanitary condition complaints over 90 days, suggesting broader sanitation issues may be enabling pest populations
reporting_angles: Is the Hunts Point food market (major neighborhood anchor) experiencing pest management failures?
Are inadequate waste collection schedules or bulky item pickup delays leaving food/debris that attracts rodents?
Request DOHMH inspection records for rodent findings in past 2 weeks to confirm distribution (residential vs. commercial)

themes_detail.label: Animal Abuse Reports Spike
themes_detail.summary: Animal abuse complaints jumped to 6 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 2.2 per week over 8 weeks—a 167% increase (z-score: 3.44)—warranting investigation into potential organized animal fighting, neglect rings, or cruelty patterns.
evidence: 6 animal abuse complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 3.44, classified as high severity
Spike is recent and isolated to one week, suggesting either acute event or emerging pattern
reporting_angles: Request NYPD and ASPCA complaint logs to determine whether reports cluster by location, suggesting organized animal fighting or a single facility failure
Investigate whether any recent evictions or building closures left animals behind or created conditions enabling abuse
Interview animal rescue organizations working in Hunts Point about trends they're observing

themes_detail.label: Heat/Hot Water Crisis Baseline
themes_detail.summary: Heat and hot water complaints dominate CD 202 at 2,334 over 90 days (25.9 complaints per day), reflecting chronic building maintenance failures; while not a NEW spike this week, the persistent volume aligns with community board's long-standing budget request for additional building inspectors, suggesting systemic landlord non-compliance.
evidence: 2,334 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days—by far the highest complaint category
Community Board has requested additional building inspectors (DOB) in repeated budget cycles, indicating unresolved systemic problem
228 total DOB permits filed in last 90 days, with 177 alterations, suggesting active building modifications—yet heat/hot water complaints remain highest priority
reporting_angles: Which landlords are repeat offenders for heat/hot water violations? Cross-reference 311 data with HPD violation history.
Why has the community board's years-long request for additional building inspectors not been fulfilled? Interview CB members and DOB leadership.
Feature resident stories about winter heating failures and health impacts
